Briefing for 8 November 2026

Short items for 8 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

Everyday tool

OpenAI raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion value

According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has closed a first $11 billion slice of a round that could reach about $20 billion. The valuation is below the $1.4 trillion it reportedly aimed for in September.

Source: TechCrunch

AI agents · More technical

DeepMind agents find two weak spots in old 1024-bit RSA

Google DeepMind says human-guided AI agents found faster signature forgery and cheaper batch factoring for legacy 1024-bit RSA. Modern keys of 2048 bits or more are not affected, and part of the work is still theoretical.

Source: Interesting Engineering

Study

OpenAI tests agents on everyday lab data

BioBasicsBench, built with biotech firm Ligo, has 100 tasks where agents read raw gels, images, and instrument output and must flag weak evidence. OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra scored 66.7%, still with gaps on controls.

Source: OpenAI

New model

Ripple-65B Preview: open coding model under Apache 2.0

Chip design firm Ricursive Intelligence released a dense 65B model on Hugging Face that it says leads open US models on TerminalBench 2.1. It trails Inkling 2 Small but should be easier to run on your own hardware.

Source: The Decoder

Everyday tool

US shoppers can now text Alexa to search and buy

Amazon is inviting selected US customers to shop with its Alexa agent by text message: search, compare, add to cart, buy, and track prices or orders. A wider rollout is planned in the coming weeks.

Source: Amazon

Everyday tool

Google's smartwatch AI spots signs of high blood pressure

In a Nature study with 196 people, a model using only smartwatch pulse and motion sensors flagged hypertension in 65.8% of cases. Google says it is a screening hint for a doctor's visit, not a diagnosis.

Source: Google Research

Device

Google takes over Crusoe's unfinished Wyoming campus

Crusoe sold its planned data center site in Wyoming to Google, which plans to invest $17 billion there. The price was not disclosed; Google had reportedly raised concerns about the project's cost and timeline.

Source: TechCrunch
